phase04aRepairRevisionNote: Phase 04A REPAIR (2026-09-21, after an independent Opus acceptance HOLD on 6b239dd found two real defects): (1) FDA-002 deleteFlag's ordering was inverted — it deleted the flags row first and cleaned up photos best-effort afterward, so a Storage failure could leave a public photo orphaned with the row already gone (the exact SR-050 takedown risk). Per Sky's D-04A-1 decision, required photo cleanup now happens BEFORE the row DELETE and is fail-closed: a Storage error, or a photo whose exact object path cannot be established (no owner uid to validate against, a foreign folder, a malformed URL), now REFUSES the delete instead of proceeding. Nothing in this repair is 'best-effort' any more — every photo this flag's rows reference must be provably removed or the row survives. (2) FDA-019's batchInsertFlagPhotos only cleaned up the ONE photo whose row-insert failed; every already-uploaded photo after it in the batch (never even attempted) was left orphaned in Storage with no DB pointer. batchInsertFlagPhotos now cleans up every unattached photo — the failing one and everything after it — on any failure, leaving already-attached photos untouched. contractManifest.guard.test.ts's FDA-002/FDA-019 sub-tests and the D1F4R3 source-closure/replay guards were updated in the same repair to assert the accepted current contract instead of the pre-04A one; see 04A-repair HANDOFF for the full predicate list.

FDA-004 (moderation-queue) is reconciled with dated evidence only, not deployed. No Phase03A/03B RPC-dependent surface (flag-status-transition, leaderboard) or FDA-003 (account-deletion, owned by 04B) changed. See each surface's phase04aNote for exact evidence and file:line citations. SUPERSEDED by phase04aRepairRevisionNote above for the flag-delete and photo-upload-flag surfaces — the delete ordering and orphan-cleanup gaps described there were found by independent review AFTER this note was written.

revisionNote: Rev 2 corrects rev 1 after independent review. Rev 1 was accurate at NAME granularity but wrong at CALL-SITE granularity: it omitted a call site, misattributed two files, classified four sites by the throw at the call rather than by what the caller does with it, and did not record the moderation-column WRITE sites at all. Classifications below are per call site and were each read at the cited line.

onAbsentDefinitions.hard: the call throws AND a user-visible action fails
onAbsentDefinitions.degraded: the call throws but the caller completes the primary action and tells the user what was lost
onAbsentDefinitions.graceful: absence is detected and a working alternative path or empty state is used
onAbsentDefinitions.swallowed: the error is caught and discarded; no user-visible effect
onAbsentDefinitions.silent: no error check at all — the failure is invisible to code and user alike
onAbsentDefinitions.unreachable: cannot be called when its prerequisite contract is absent
onAbsentDefinitions.fail_closed: the capability is withheld with a warning and no permissive fallback
onAbsentDefinitions.optional_omitted: the call fails but successfully loaded primary content remains visible while optional dependent content is omitted

surfaces.phase04aRepairNote: Phase 04A REPAIR (2026-09-21): independent review found the legacy fallback above could orphan Storage objects on a multi-photo submit — batchInsertFlagPhotos (photos.ts) only cleaned up the ONE photo whose flag_photos row-insert failed; every already-uploaded photo AFTER it in the same batch (never even attempted) was left as a real object in the flag-photos bucket with no DB row pointing at it, for any batch mixing intent-based and legacy uploads. Repaired: on any attach failure, every not-yet-attached photo from that point on is now cleaned up too (cancelFlagPhotoUpload for intent-based uploads, removeUploadedFlagPhotos for legacy ones) — already-attached photos before the failure are left untouched. See src/lib/__tests__/photos.test.ts's 'FDA-019 orphan repair' suite (failure at first/middle/final position, mixed intent+legacy) for the behavioral proof.

surfaces.phase04aNote: Phase 04A (2026-09-21): deleteFlag no longer calls the undeployed delete-flag Edge Function (P04-D01, accepted 2026-09-03 — do not deploy D1F4 merely to satisfy the client). It now issues a strict direct Data API DELETE authorized entirely by the live RLS below, requires a returned id (zero rows = FlagDeleteRefusedError, never a silent/false success). SUPERSEDED by phase04aRepairNote below — the original implementation cleaned up photos best-effort AFTER the row delete; that ordering was found unsafe by independent review and has been repaired.
surfaces.phase04aRepairNote: Phase 04A REPAIR (2026-09-21, Sky's D-04A-1 decision): required photo cleanup now happens BEFORE the row DELETE and fails closed on any problem — it is never optional or deferred to a later sweep. deleteFlag now (1) determines every Storage object this flag's photos require removed, (2) refuses the delete outright (FlagDeleteRefusedError) if any required photo's exact path cannot be established — no owner uid to validate a legacy URL against, a foreign-folder URL, or a malformed one — since that means required absence cannot be proven, (3) removes every required object and refuses the delete if that Storage call errors (removeRequiredFlagPhotos throws; nothing here is swallowed), and ONLY THEN (4) issues the flags DELETE, validating that the returned rows actually contain the intended flagId (not merely a non-zero length). This closes the SR-050 public-photo-orphan risk the original delete-the-row-then-clean-up-afterward ordering left open, at the cost of an anonymous flag's uncleanable legacy photo now making that flag undeletable until a server-side sweep resolves it — an accepted, explicit trade-off under D-04A-1, not an oversight. The 2026-09-04 deployed-contract.v1.json capture independently confirmed 'flags delete own', 'admin delete any flag', 'flag-photos owner delete', and 'flag-photos admin delete' all live (authorization.flagsPolicies / storage.objectPolicies).

callSites.name: flags
callSites.note: DELETE ... RETURNING id, issued ONLY after every required photo object is proven removed (or none were required). A returned-rows set that is empty OR does not contain this exact flagId throws FlagDeleteRefusedError; this client never infers owner/admin privilege itself.
